facts.claim: Children who were regularly exposed to lavender or tea tree essential oils experienced the same risk of endocrine disorders as those who were not exposed.
facts.quote: Children who were regularly exposed to lavender or tea tree essential oils experienced the same risk of endocrine disorders as those who were not exposed.

facts.claim: The total risk of endocrine disorders among children exposed to lavender or tea tree essential oils (0.0194) did not differ from the risk of those unexposed (0.0069).
facts.quote: Total risk of endocrine disorders among those exposed (0.0194) did not differ from the risk of those unexposed (0.0069).

facts.claim: 31 essential oils of culinary herbs and spices may be considered safe in terms of endocrine disruption involving receptors GR, AR and VDR.
facts.quote: Hence, 31 EOs of culinary herbs and spices may be considered safe, in terms of endocrine disruption involving receptors GR, AR and VDR.

facts.claim: Cases of premature thelarche resolved upon cessation of lavender-containing fragrance exposure commonly used in Hispanic communities.
facts.quote: We report cases of premature thelarche that resolved upon cessation of lavender-containing fragrance exposure commonly used in Hispanic communities.

facts.claim: The toxicological significance of the minor effects observed on transcriptional activities of GR, AR and VDR is very low.
facts.quote: In conclusion, although we observed minor effects of several EOs on transcriptional activities of GR, AR and VDR, the toxicological significance of these effects is very low.

facts.claim: The largest source of general population exposure to phthalates is dietary.
facts.quote: The largest source of general population exposure to phthalates is dietary.

research.angle: While some essential oil components show estrogenic properties and are linked to specific cases of premature breast growth in children, large-scale studies show that regular exposure to common oils like lavender and tea tree does not significantly increase the risk of endocrine disorders compared to unexposed groups.
research.verdict: The evidence is mixed, showing that while specific components can have endocrine-disrupting activities in laboratory settings or specific clinical cases, they do not consistently cause endocrine disorders in the general population.
research.caveat: The studies vary significantly in scope, ranging from small case reports of specific conditions to large population-based prevalence studies.
